status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Calendar, the one flow factor and the production rule, climate, weather, the slice's gates and events (the trader's visits, the farm family's market days, the muster), what can be gathered when (forage), and the default era.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify

start_default.name: Peace start
start_default.why: An autumn start runs the credit year: the fall outfit, the winter's furs, the spring settlement. In 1765 Johnson was applying parts of the Plan of 1764 administratively (trade only at posts, commissaries, tariffs); Parliament never enacted the plan, and the Crown returned regulation to the colonies in 1768. The small post at the ford keeps a detachment of regulars in what may be its last season (a composite: map_regions.json reg.fort_clearing).

calendar.rule: Every per-year rate in the data derives from days_per_year; there are no alternative year lengths (review 2, issue 17).
calendar.slice_span_rule: The slice runs from Early September 1765 to the close of the spring settlement window (Early May 1766): M1 is one winter night inside it, M2 the whole credit year.

time.rule: ONE conversion factor for everything produced and consumed: a game day of eating, work, wages, board, hire and trap nights stands for 5 days of the same (items' game kcal, wages, trap nights). The calendar only names the date: a game day covers about ten calendar days of the season, so the year turns in 36 game days.
time.season_total_rule: A once-a-year total (a harvest, a whole sugar season, a whole fish run) is multiplied by 0.49 (= 5 x 36 / 365), so what a year produces keeps its historical ratio to what a year eats: an acre of corn feeds a player about as many game years as it fed a person calendar years. The slice has no such totals; the backlog uses this rule for harvests, sugaring and fish runs.
time.durations: Spoilage, drying, healing and illness durations are explicit game days in each item and condition row. There is no process rule and no second or third clock (review 2 of v2, the clocks issue).
time.per_use_prices: Goods and services bought per item or per use keep colonial cash prices (economy.json).

production_rule.rule: The flow factor applies to gathering and making too: yield = historical rate per hour x game hours x 5; hands-on craft time = historical hands-on hours / 5; passive waits (soaking, drying, curing) are game days per row. A node's stock for the season is a once-a-year total (season_total_scale).
production_rule.stage_rule: No job stage is longer than 120 game minutes: the half-faced camp and snowshoes are made in resumable stages (and in co-op every stage stays under the personal lead).
production_rule.retune: Several backlog yields and times predate this rule and are retuned when their rows go live (redesign_economy.md 9.3).

time_of_day.gameplay_light: SimClock publishes light_level 0-1 from the date, daylight_h and weather; survival checks (mod.night_no_light), detection and night activities read it.
time_of_day.visuals: Until the visuals workflow agrees an interface, time of day is gameplay-only. The environment rig (scripts/world/env/environment_rig.gd, a frozen API owned by another package) keeps its fixed sun and writes the wind globals in build(). Proposed interface: the rig reads SimClock, or exposes set_time_of_day(hours) and set_wind(direction, strength) for Weather to call (review 2, issue 13).

climate.rule: Month temperatures are Albany 1991-2020 NOAA normals (N:28) plus -2 C [D/M]; regions add their offsets and snow multipliers below.

region_offsets.rule: Region air = month curve + temp_c; snow depth = month depth x snow_depth_mult.

reg.fort_clearing.note: the upper Mohawk at the ford, on the edge of the lake-effect snow belt

pelt_prime_by_species.note: Per-species prime curves (review 1, issue 18). Beaver, muskrat, otter and mink taken after ice-out stay good into April and early May; the spring hunt was a major season. Fur pelts only (items.json pelt_rules).

states.note: fresh snow shows tracks, then fills them

weather.temperature_rule: air = lerp(low, high, day curve) + region temp_c + state temp_add + noise(+-3)
weather.wind: Weather computes gameplay wind (scent, arrow drift, smoke). It does not claim the wind_direction and wind_strength shader globals, which the environment rig writes; see time_of_day.visuals.
weather.weapon_effects: misfire_add applies to an uncovered lock (item.tool.lock_cover prevents it); a damp bowstring gives bow_power_mult 0.9

trapping_season.note: furs prime from December to February

backcountry_hunt.note: settler hunters out for the season

fall_mast.note: nuts and acorns on the ground

ice_fishing.note: river ice 10 cm or more: January and February in the slice (months.river_ice_cm)

ground_open.rule: the ground is not frozen (not winter below 0 C): roots can be dug

events.name: Fall credit
events.effects: The Schenectady trader comes up with the last boats of the season and outfits hunters on his book against the spring; an account unpaid last spring means no outfit now (economy.json credit).

events.name: The winter's firewood
events.effects: The lieutenant lets the garrison's winter firewood by the cord (livelihoods.json job.garrison_firewood).

events.name: Winter quarters
events.effects: The detachment goes into winter quarters; the sutler's store is the warm room of the post.

events.name: The trader's winter visit
events.effects: The trader comes up the valley road by sleigh for two days: buys furs and skins, takes payments on the book, sells from a small stock (review 2 of v2, the missing-buyer blocker).

events.name: The trader's late-winter visit
events.effects: The last sleigh before the thaw: furs, skins and payments, and the almanac's warning that the book falls due in the spring window.

events.name: The spring settlement
events.effects: The first bateaux after the ice: the trader weighs the winter's furs and settles every book. The window runs from Mid April to Early May; the almanac warns from Mid March (economy.json credit.grading).

events.name: The district's spring muster
events.effects: The district's militia company musters on the fort's parade by the lieutenant's leave: a game day. backgrounds.json obligation_rules say who does what.

events.name: The farm family's harvest visit
events.effects: A farm family from German Flatts comes to the post after the harvest with cornmeal, flour, salt pork, sauerkraut and dried apples to trade.

events.name: The farm family comes by sleigh
events.effects: The farm family comes up by sleigh: cornmeal and kraut for meat and skins.

events.name: The farm family in the hungry time
events.effects: The farm family comes in the hungry time, short of meat and with little cornmeal left.

events.name: The farm family at the muster
events.effects: The farm family comes with the district's muster, the last of their stores in the wagon.

eras.notes: Johnson applies parts of the Plan of 1764 administratively from 1765 (trade confined to posts under commissaries, tariffs, licences); Parliament never enacted the plan, and in 1768 the Crown returns regulation to the colonies. Kirkland's mission at the Oneida town from 1766. The communication posts are being given up one by one.

plan_1764.text: The Plan of 1764 as Johnson applied it administratively: Indian trade at posts under commissaries, with tariffs and licences, enforced unevenly. Never enacted by Parliament; ended in 1768 when regulation returned to the colonies. In the slice it touches only the trader's licence and posted prices, not the colonial hunter's own sales.

almanac.rule: The slice's almanac is one journal page: the date, the trader's next visit, the farm family's market days, the soldiers' evenings and the old hunter's away weeks, the winter-ready checklist, and the settlement window and its warning only while an account is open.

forage_rule: forage.search takes the easiest row in season at a node in reach and draws its yield from the node's season stock (map_regions.json resource_nodes); yields follow the production rule.
